selectionGuidance:
Learning-first, representation-aware authoring: learning objective → knowledge structure → learner action → candidate section capabilities → representation and configuration → focused contracts → OUI and narration → validation/repair → delivery. Choose the simplest representation or complementary combination that fully supports the intended learning experience. Native Loom sections and OpenUI are first-class choices; there is no section ranking, visual quota or mandatory sequence.

Compare candidates by knowledge fidelity (preserve information and relationships), learner action (what the learner does), perspective coverage (what additional views reveal), cognitive clarity (avoid unnecessary complexity), assessment suitability (what response demonstrates the outcome) and authoring feasibility (what the evidence can actually model). Record the choice in TopicPlan activity, rationale and presentation.strategy before retrieving exact signatures. Resolve relevant advisory warnings or explicitly justify proceeding; structural validity alone is not experience readiness.

Bullets teach numbered linear procedures, checklists, prerequisites, key points, supporting details and concise summaries. They are distinct from Text. OpenUI Steps add visual stage guidance; Flowchart teaches interactions, responsibilities, messages, data or states, even in a linear process when perspectives add understanding. Reflection Sequence practises order; User Journey follows a person's experience. Text is appropriate for connected prose, nuanced explanation and argument; consider alternatives when they clarify the objective, without forcing interactivity.

Flashcards introduce definitions and meanings as well as practise recall. OpenUI cards/stacks compare examples, tables compare factual attributes, labelled Svg diagrams explain spatial structure, and charts explain quantities or trends. Empirical charts require supplied or verified data; clearly label illustrative data and never invent benchmark results. Tradeoff Sandbox evaluates options and decisions; Formula Sandbox explores parameter sensitivity. Select the other native sections by their learning purpose below.

For full lessons, combine sections only when each adds a distinct contribution: e.g. Flowchart explains RAG tool execution, Bullets guides implementation, Scenario explores retrieval failures and Quiz assesses application. Distinguish presentation, exploration and assessment. Viewing, clicking, switching views and flipping cards are engagement, not demonstrated mastery.

Retrieve selected section rules, then library-scoped component contracts and dependencies. If focused retrieval fails, retry with the correct library and forceRefresh; then use the selected legacy section guide (omit library/components). For OpenUI, retrieve its section guide and selected component families. If contracts remain unavailable, report the blocker and revise/revalidate the plan only to an equally faithful supported representation; never silently downgrade to Text or invent signatures.

openuiVisuals.learningGoal: Compare concrete examples or evidence layouts side by side
openuiVisuals.components: Card / Stack with concise explanations or labelled Svg drawings

openuiVisuals.learningGoal: Show an amount developing over time
openuiVisuals.components: AreaChart; use cumulative data when teaching accumulation

openuiVisuals.learningGoal: Show flat shares of one whole

openuiVisuals.components: ScatterChart; an association alone does not establish causation

openuiVisuals.learningGoal: Look up or compare factual attributes
Explain spatial structure, anatomy, a mechanism or a concrete analogy

sections.summary: Topic opener: what it is, why it matters, and a roadmap of the sections ahead. `displayTitle` overrides the title shown inside the card.
sections.selectionQuestion: What will I learn, why does it matter, and where are we going?

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Read the purpose and roadmap.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Orient attention; keep the opening focused.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Reading is engagement, not demonstrated understanding.

sections.summary: Prose section: one string per paragraph.
sections.selectionQuestion: Does this idea need connected prose or narrative? Before choosing Text, consider native sections and OpenUI comparisons, diagrams, tables or charts; use prose when it best teaches the goal.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Read a connected explanation or argument.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Keep prose readable in Read and Present; check long paragraphs at phone width.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Prose can be the right representation; viewing it is not assessment.

sections.summary: Linear instructions, prerequisites, checklists, key points and summaries; set `ordered` true for numbered procedures.
sections.mentalModel: Linear procedures, prerequisites, checklists and key points
sections.selectionQuestion: Can concise numbered steps, a checklist, supporting details or a summary teach this clearly?

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Follow numbered instructions, check prerequisites or inspect key points and supporting details.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Use documented item beats; avoid turning every item into a paragraph wall.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: A checklist presentation does not demonstrate procedural skill.

sections.summary: Browsable taxonomy of categories with scope, analogy and details.
sections.selectionQuestion: What kinds exist, what defines them, and how do I recognise their differences?

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Select categories and inspect their distinctions.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Use focused category beats instead of a dense classification dump.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Category exploration is engagement, not a classification test.

sections.summary: Gallery of captioned images.
sections.selectionQuestion: What does it look like? Compare examples, textures, objects or screenshots.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Inspect and compare visual examples.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Check image labels and legibility at the actual viewport.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Visual inspection alone does not establish recognition accuracy.

sections.summary: Layer-stack map: layers as rows (foundation last), blocks placed on a gap-free grid. Give blocks `dependsOn` so readers can tap a block to trace what it needs and what it affects. `displayTitle` overrides the title shown inside the map.
sections.selectionQuestion: What builds on or is supported by what? Examples include network layers or cloud foundation → agent runtime → application.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Inspect layers and what each foundation supports.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Keep layer labels short and inspect the complete stack in Read.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Layer inspection alone does not demonstrate dependency reasoning.

sections.summary: A person’s experience across product or service stages. Read explores stages; Present walks goals, actions, responses and optional friction and outcomes without an Event Storming diagram.
sections.mentalModel: A person’s experience with a product or service
sections.selectionQuestion: What does the person want, do and experience at each stage, and how can friction be resolved?

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Inspect stages, goals, friction and improvements in a person’s journey.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Focus on one stage at a time; check horizontal content remains reachable.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Stage selection is exploration, not evidence of diagnosing friction.

sections.summary: Measured task timeline: one row per activity, sorted by start time, with duration-scaled bars, parallel work and finish-to-start dependencies. Present keeps the whole diagram visible while focusing authored groups.
sections.mentalModel: Measured time, duration, overlap and waiting
sections.selectionQuestion: When does each task start and finish, what runs together, and what must wait?

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Inspect start times, durations, overlap and waiting.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Time geometry must use authored measurements; verify labels and scale.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Selection is exploration; interpretation needs a learner response.

sections.summary: A whole divided into measurable parts: costs, counts, time allocation or conditional probability. Calculates each part’s share of its parent and the whole, validates totals, and explains one split per presentation beat.
sections.mentalModel: Parts of a measurable whole and conditional probability
sections.selectionQuestion: How does a total divide through a hierarchy? Use quantity mode for costs/counts and probability mode for conditional branches and path probabilities.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Explore how a quantity or probability divides through branches.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Preserve visible totals and branch labels; inspect deep trees in Read.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Expansion is engagement; it does not establish quantitative reasoning.

sections.summary: Animated Event Storming flowchart. Every actor and system must be used by at least one step.
sections.selectionQuestion: What happens, what triggers it, who handles it, and how do participants interact? Choose the view from the table below.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Step through events, responsibilities and handoffs in the appropriate view.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Select the documented process view and inspect graph labels at the viewport.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Stepping through a process is engagement; test application separately.

views.purpose: Event → policy → command → system → resulting event; explain triggers and rules.
Components, their responsibilities and their connections.
Who sends what to whom, and in what order; vertical spacing is not measured duration.
How events change the state of something.

capabilities.narration: Flowchart.initialView selects the primary view; NarrationStep.view may change views on the same beat for a distinct teaching purpose.
capabilities.modelingConstraints: Use real participants and event → policy → command → handler → event cycles. Data Flow uses Event.data; State Machine requires StateMachine and Event.enters. JourneyStep.processGroup is a phase label, not a state. Never invent model detail to activate views.

sections.summary: Branching "what would you do?" scenario. `startNode` defaults to "start". `displayTitle` overrides the title shown inside the scenario.
sections.selectionQuestion: What happens if I choose this, then make another decision? Explore authored paths and outcomes.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Choose authored decisions and inspect consequences.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Present demonstrates paths; Read permits learner decisions.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: An explored consequence is not independently verified mastery.

sections.summary: Interactive sandbox where learners make design choices and watch metrics move.
sections.mentalModel: Presenting options, comparing alternatives and trade-offs
sections.selectionQuestion: What are my options, how do they compare, and when should I choose each? Show strengths, limitations, gains, costs and suitability; a recommendation can explain why an option fits. Use this for option comparison even without formal mathematical optimisation.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Compare options, strengths, costs and suitability for a situation.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Present guides option comparisons; Read supports learner exploration.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Exploring options does not prove a justified decision.

sections.summary: Parameter sandbox: sliders drive live formula-based metrics.
sections.selectionQuestion: How does changing an input change a calculated result? Let the learner vary inputs to an authored formula.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Vary inputs and observe authored calculated outputs.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Present demonstrates chosen inputs; Read is needed for learner experiments.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Slider movement is engagement, not correctness or causal understanding.

sections.summary: Interactive decision guide. `root` is the ID of the first node. `displayTitle` overrides the title shown inside the guide.
sections.selectionQuestion: Which option fits my situation after answering a sequence of questions?

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Answer branching questions to inspect a rule-based recommendation.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Present demonstrates a path; Read lets the learner choose branches.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: A reached recommendation is not an assessment score.

sections.summary: Sequence-builder reflection: learners put steps in the right order.
sections.selectionQuestion: Can I arrange the supplied steps into the correct sequence?

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Reconstruct the order of supplied steps and check the answer.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Present demonstrates reconstruction; Read supports learner attempts.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Correctness concerns this authored sequence, not general mastery.

sections.summary: Self-explanation reflection: learners complete sentence templates with chips.
sections.selectionQuestion: Can I complete a sound explanation using the supplied concepts and sentence blanks?

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Complete an explanation from supplied concepts and sentence blanks.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Present demonstrates a completed explanation; use Read for attempts.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Explicit results concern this exercise, not independent free-text reasoning.

sections.summary: Knowledge-check section of multiple-choice questions.
sections.selectionQuestion: Can I answer or apply what has already been taught?

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Submit an answer and inspect authored feedback.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Present demonstrates answers; Read captures learner attempts.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Explicit correct/wrong attempts are evidence; views and stage demonstrations are not mastery.

sections.summary: Deck of flip cards for key vocabulary.
sections.selectionQuestion: What does this term or concept mean? Teach its meaning on the back of a card, then use it for recall; flashcards introduce concepts as well as practise them.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Try recall, then flip to inspect a definition or example.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Present demonstrates front/back; use Read for learner-controlled recall.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: A flip records exposure, not correctness of unauthored recall.

sections.summary: Knowledge graph of concepts and the relations between them.
sections.selectionQuestion: How do ideas connect, depend on, support or differ from each other? Label the relationship explicitly.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Inspect concepts and their labelled relationships.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Check that labels and connections remain readable at phone width.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: A displayed relationship does not show the learner can explain it.

sections.summary: Free-form layout from the standard OpenUI library: cards, tabs, tables, charts and Svg drawings.
sections.mentalModel: Composed visual explanation, comparison and data
sections.selectionQuestion: Would a chart, table, simple procedure, drawing, analogy or mixed composition express this idea best? See the visual choices below.

learningBehavior.learnerAction: Inspect or interact with an authored composition of cards, diagrams, tables or charts.
learningBehavior.presentationConstraint: Use supported child beats and narration targets; measure dense tables/charts at phone width.
learningBehavior.evidenceBoundary: Component presence is not proof of meaningful interaction. Use verified or labelled illustrative chart data; static tables are valid for factual comparison.
